per_shot.note: Furnished hall reads as lived in: lit book shelf, bright orrery-style star chart with picture light, arc lamp pool, porthole dusk; lower third of floor is a big blotchy empty plane.
Fern, desk, and radio with a clearly glowing dial all read; lower-wall panel grid adds structure; rug is only a corner.

Rug pattern reads well, and the shelf light lands on the spines so the books look cared for; the rug's thick slab edge looks like a plinth, and there is a stray green smear on the floor at lower left.
Star chart is the strongest item: luminous orbits under a picture light. Arc lamp throws a clear warm pool on wall and floor; galley is cropped at the right edge.
Kettle, cups, tile backsplash, tea towel, bunk with pillow and blanket, and the glowing sconce pool make a warm vignette; the kettle glows like a lantern instead of reading as metal.
Distinct cool room with dark slatted wainscot and teal trim; cold white fixtures make it feel more like a lab than a sanctuary.
Warm pink-copper walls with a brass mid-rail and a dark lower band make a cosy, distinct mood that sits well with the dusk portholes.
Best palette: olive panels over a vertical-board wood wainscot with a rail read as a different room, not a recolour.

top_issues.why: In the mid shot, roughly the bottom 35% of the frame is soft light blotches on plain plates. That dilutes how rich the furnished room feels.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give the plating a seam/inset pattern with value steps, or a runner or threshold strip, and keep the warm pools tighter under their sources.

top_issues.issue: Kettle reads as an emissive lamp
top_issues.why: A bright orange glowing kettle competes with the sconce and stops reading as a copper object.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Drop its emissive and let the shelf light give it a specular highlight. Add a thin wisp of steam if it should feel 'on'.

top_issues.issue: Rug edge looks like a raised slab
top_issues.why: The thick light-coloured edge and side make the woven rug look like a board or plinth.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Thin the rug to near-floor height with a darker edge, and keep the fringe.

top_issues.issue: Palettes share identical furniture and lighting temperature apart from fixtures
top_issues.why: The wall treatments differ, but floor and ceiling only tint. Slate's cold fixtures push it toward clinical rather than sanctuary.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give each palette its own floor tone/trim accent and keep at least one warm practical in Slate so it stays a home.

top_issues.issue: Radio and galley cropped at the frame edges in the mid shot
top_issues.why: At play scale, the radio and galley are mostly off frame, so the full room undersells the bought items.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Camera framing is out of scope. Make sure each item has a clear small glow or silhouette so it registers even when partly in frame.

protect: Star chart with picture light and luminous orbit rings
Shelf strip-light landing on the book spines
Per-palette wall structure (Verdant wood wainscot, Rose brass rail, Slate slatted lower wall)
Warm arc-lamp pool and dusk portholes
Suit remains the brightest, clearest figure

per_shot.note: Same room, but the star chart is dim and muted with no picture light. The glossy floor adds streak reflections, including a teal smear under the console.
Fern, desk and radio read; dial glow slightly weaker and lower-wall panel grid gone, flatter wall.
Rug sits flatter and reads more like a rug, but there is no shelf light, so the books sit in shadow. A teal reflection smears under the suit.
Star chart is a dark field of faint dots with no light on it, so it barely reads as a prized item. The lamp pool is weaker on the floor; the cream locker reads cleanly.
Kettle reads correctly as a dark copper object, and the bunk and cups read. The sconce is much dimmer, so the bunk corner is less cosy.
Distinct cool room, but the lower wall is plain and the star chart nearly disappears. The reflective floor adds some interest.
Pleasant pink-copper tone, but without the mid-rail it is closer to a flat recolour; the floor reflections are warm.
Green over a plain red-brown lower band; it loses A's wood wainscot and rail, so it reads more as a tint swap.

top_issues.issue: Star chart lost its light and presence
top_issues.why: A muted, unlit dark rectangle doesn't read as a cared-for star chart at play scale.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Restore a picture light and the brighter orbit rings and constellation points.

top_issues.issue: Practicals on the bought items are weaker
top_issues.why: Without the shelf light, and with a dimmer sconce, the books and bunk get less warm light. The brief asks for light that lands warmly.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Bring back the shelf strip-light and the brighter bunk sconce pool.

top_issues.why: Without the per-palette rail and wainscot treatments, each palette is mostly a hue shift of the same flat panels.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give each palette its own wall structure: wood wainscot, brass rail, slatted lower wall.

top_issues.issue: Reflective floor streaks and teal smear
top_issues.why: Long vertical reflection streaks and a teal ghost under the console and suit look like a wet, glossy lab floor rather than hab plating, and they add noise beside the suit.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Lower the floor gloss and roughen it so the warm pools stay soft. Suppress the teal emissive reflection.

protect: Kettle as a non-emissive copper object

why: A's items are better lit and read better: star chart, books and bunk sconce. Its palettes have real structural differences, not just a tint. B only wins on the kettle material and the rug profile.
